record.evidence_text: astronauts moving between different gravitational fields—say, the microgravity of a spacecraft, to the low gravity of the Moon, back to the spacecraft, and then back to Earth—may also have weakened bones and muscles that heighten injury risk
landing, in particular, creates injury risk that scientists work to counter

NASA scientists are building human body models to help characterize how the body is affected in various spaceflight environments. These models help scientists develop the best standards for vehicle designs to reduce injury risks (for instance, standards on seat configurations and the restraints crews use to "strap in" during landing)

object.name: vehicle design standards (e.g., seat configurations and restraints)
